name: Collect customer payments
summary: Credit and collections analysts work the receivables that do not clear on their own: invoices past their due date, payments that arrive short or without a usable remittance, and invoices the customer has disputed. They check the invoice's status in the customer's e-invoicing network, send statements and reminders, phone customers' payables staff, and pass disputes to account managers. Collections are slow because producers pay on long cycles and only after invoice approval, and because a few large customers hold much of the balance; when a producer gets into financial trouble the company puts the account on hold, may register a builders' lien against the well, and sometimes writes the debt off.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian pressure pumping company with more than 60 producer customers, one of which holds 35-40% of receivables, and a five-person credit and collections team in the Calgary finance department.
baseline.notes: Common practice of large WCSB pressure pumpers in 2019-2022: an ERP with billing, AR and AP modules, tablet field ticketing linked to the price book, customer e-invoicing networks (mainly OpenInvoice), OCR scanning of supplier invoices, email, phone and Excel. No machine-learning coding or matching.

unit_of_work: one collection follow-up (an overdue, short-paid or disputed invoice taken up by the credit team)
trigger: The weekly aging run flags an invoice past its due date, or the daily cash application leaves a payment short, unapplied or with a deduction.
end_state: The cash is applied and the invoice cleared, or the balance is written off with approval.

volume.seasonality: Rises two to three months after the winter peak (April to June) as winter invoices come due, and in 2020 when producers stretched payments and some failed.

evidence.note: About 620 invoices a month (trican-mda-2022). Year-end receivables of 68-75 days of revenue suggest that a large share of invoices pass their 30-60 day terms; about 40% of invoices are assumed to need at least one follow-up, matching the organisation file's 250 a month.

About 45 minutes of hands-on work per follow-up over about 250 a month is about 1.5 FTE; the rest of the five analysts' time goes to applying every customer payment, credit limit reviews and the weekly aging report.
Settles disputes and escalates with customers on about one case in four.
Raises credit memos agreed in disputes.
Approves credit memos, credit holds and write-offs.
Prepares and registers builders' liens for a few cases a month.

systems.name: ERP (finance, procurement, inventory, plant maintenance, billing)
Customer e-invoicing and field ticket approval networks
Email, Microsoft Teams and mobile phones
Business intelligence dashboards on ERP and job data

steps.name: Aging run puts the item on the collections list
steps.description: Each week the ERP aging report lists invoices past their due date by customer, and each day the bank file of EFT and cheque payments is matched to open invoices; items that cannot be matched in full drop into the credit analyst's worklist.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Check the invoice status with the customer's network
steps.description: The credit analyst looks the invoice up in the customer's e-invoicing network and the ERP: whether it was approved, is still with an approver, was rejected, or is scheduled for a payment run, and whether a remittance came in.

next.condition: no status or stuck with an approver

evidence.note: Suppliers monitor invoice status in OpenInvoice (cenovus-invoicing). Shares and times tier C.

steps.name: Wait for the customer's payment run
steps.description: Approved invoices are paid in the producer's next scheduled payment run, often weekly or twice a month and on the producer's own terms counted from approval rather than from the invoice date.

next.condition: not paid in the expected run

evidence.note: Producers commonly pay at about 90 days and some later (yager-2015). Waits tier C.

steps.name: Research a short or unapplied payment
steps.description: The analyst reads the remittance advice from the customer's network or email, matches the payment to invoices, and works out any deduction: a disputed line, a credit taken twice, a GST difference or an invoice the customer never received.

error.defect_description: Payment applied to the wrong invoice.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Send a statement and reminder
steps.description: The analyst emails the customer's payables contact a statement of overdue invoices with copies of the invoices and signed tickets, asking for a payment date.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Customer replies, pays or stays silent
steps.description: The customer's payables team checks its system and pays, replies with a reason such as a missing approval or a dispute, or does not answer.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Phone the customer and escalate
steps.description: The analyst phones the customer's payables lead, and if there is still no commitment asks the account manager to raise it with the customer's operations contact.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Log the dispute and pass it on
steps.description: The analyst records the dispute reason and amount in the collections notes and sends it to the account manager, copying billing, with the invoice, tickets and the customer's comment.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Account manager resolves the dispute
steps.description: The account manager discusses the disputed price, quantity or standby with the customer's completions or drilling lead, using the signed ticket and tender pricing, and agrees that the charge stands, that a credit is due, or that it needs escalation.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Escalate with the customer's management
steps.description: At the weekly aging meeting the account manager, credit team and controller review the oldest balances; the account manager then calls a senior contact at the customer, sometimes tying payment to further work.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Raise the credit memo
steps.description: A billing specialist prepares the credit memo in the ERP for the agreed amount, referencing the original invoice, the dispute notes and the account manager's email confirming the agreement.

error.defect_description: Credit amount or invoice reference wrong.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Controller approves the credit memo
steps.description: The controller checks the credit memo against the dispute notes and approves it, after which the customer is told and the remaining balance is collected.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: credit memos approved by someone other than the preparer

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Review the customer's credit exposure
steps.description: The analyst pulls the customer's total balance, aging, credit limit, recent payment pattern and public news or a credit report, and summarises the exposure, including work booked for the coming weeks.

evidence.note: Customer credit risk depends on commodity prices and producers' financing; one customer held 35-40% of receivables (trican-mda-2022). Times tier C.

steps.name: Decide on credit hold, lien or write-off
steps.description: The controller, with the account manager's input, decides whether to put the account on hold for new work, register a lien against the well, keep collecting, or provide for and write off the balance when the producer is insolvent.

control.basis: Company credit policy: credit holds and liens approved by the corporate controller

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Register a builders' lien against the well
steps.description: Legal counsel prepares a statement of lien for the unpaid well work and registers it against the producer's mineral lease with the Minister of Energy within 90 days of the last work, then diarises the 180-day deadline for a lis pendens and an action.

control.basis: Builders' Lien Act (Alberta): liens for work on an oil or gas well registered within 90 days; lis pendens within 180 days

evidence.note: 90-day registration with the Minister of Energy and 180-day lis pendens (bj-liens-2014). Share and times tier C.

steps.name: Wait for settlement or insolvency outcome
steps.description: The producer pays to clear the lien, negotiates a settlement, or enters receivership or CCAA proceedings, in which case the company files a claim and waits for the distribution.

evidence.note: Liens on mineral interests can give weak security because they do not attach to sale proceeds (bj-liens-2014). Shares and times tier C.

steps.name: Apply the cash and clear the invoice
steps.description: The analyst applies the payment to the invoice in the ERP, clears any approved credit memo against it and notes the collection in the follow-up log.

error.defect_description: Cash applied to the wrong invoice.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Approve the write-off
steps.description: The controller approves writing off the balance against the expected credit loss allowance, with support from legal for insolvent customers, and the analyst posts the entry.

control.basis: IFRS 9 expected credit loss allowance and company write-off approval limits, reviewed by the external auditor

evidence.note: Expected credit losses measured with a provision matrix (trican-mda-2022). Times tier C.

exceptions.name: Short payment or deduction
exceptions.description: A payment arrives short or without remittance; the analyst researches and disputes the deduction.

exceptions.name: Disputed invoice and credit
exceptions.description: The customer disputes a charge; the account manager agrees a credit and a credit memo is approved.

exceptions.name: Escalation to customer management
exceptions.description: No reply to reminders and calls; the account manager escalates with the customer's management.

exceptions.name: Distressed producer: lien and write-off
exceptions.description: A producer in financial trouble is put on credit hold, a lien is registered and part is written off.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the item entering the collections list to cash applied or write-off
benchmarks.population: Overdue and short-paid producer invoices at a WCSB pressure pumper, 2019-2022 (estimate)

evidence.note: Estimate. Year-end receivables of 68-75 days of revenue (trican-mda-2022) against producer payment cycles of 60-90 days or more (yager-2015) imply most overdue items clear within a few weeks of follow-up, with a long tail of disputes and distressed customers.

pain_points.description: Producers pay only after invoice approval and on their own long cycles, so many items are 'overdue' only because they are still with an approver.

evidence.note: Long producer payment cycles in Canadian oilfield services.

pain_points.description: Remittances arrive in portals and emails in different formats, so short payments and deductions take research.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

pain_points.description: Disputes depend on account managers who are often with customers or on bids, and credit memos need controller approval.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB oilfield service billing and finance operations, 2019-2022.

pain_points.description: Concentration in one large customer and producer distress in 2019-2020 made credit decisions and liens slow and high-stakes.

evidence.note: Customer concentration and weak lien security.

sources.title: Trican Well Service Ltd. Management's Discussion and Analysis for the year ended December 31, 2022
sources.supports: A job is typically represented by an invoice and invoice frequency depends on how often the customer asks to be billed during a project; 7,625 jobs in 2022 and 7,291 in 2021; Q4 2022 revenue $236.5 million and Q4 2021 $156.4 million; trade and other receivables $175.4 million at December 31, 2022 and $127.8 million at December 31, 2021; trade and other payables $90.9 million at December 31, 2022; Q4 2022 direct costs $133.4 million; more than 60 customers; one customer 40% of accounts receivable in 2022 (35% in 2021) and 31% of revenue; expected credit losses measured with a provision matrix; working capital and credit facilities cover timing differences between cash collections and payments.

sources.title: Invoicing for suppliers
sources.supports: No paper invoices; for OpenInvoice purchase orders suppliers submit field tickets for approval, monitor OpenInvoice for approved field tickets and only then submit invoices from them; back-up such as daily time tickets attached; invoices against approved goods receipts; WBS/AFE and work order coding formats that must be entered in OpenInvoice. Current page; describes the practice of a large Canadian producer.

sources.title: The Broken Payment Model That Costs The Oil Industry Millions
sources.supports: Canadian oilfield services commentary (July 2015): the field ticket is prepared by the contractor's representative and signed by the producer's representative; the invoice must be perfect to be paid; payment delays follow when billing procedures are not followed; three-month payment is an accepted norm and some producers will not pay before 90 and possibly 120 days; many vendors carry receivables over 90 days.

sources.title: Oil, Gas, Mines, Minerals: Security under the Alberta Builders' Lien Act
sources.supports: A lien against a mineral interest for work on an oil or gas well or well site generally must be registered within 90 days of the last work or materials; liens on Crown mineral leases are registered with the Minister of Energy; a certificate of lis pendens and an action are needed within 180 days or the lien expires; the lien does not attach to sale proceeds, so security can be weak.

assumptions: Loaded costs are the organisation file's (base wage x 1.35).

Routine cash application of the roughly 620 payments a month that match automatically is not a case here; only exceptions and overdue items are. Credit analyst FTE is set above the hands-on estimate to cover it.
Billing specialists (credit memos) and legal counsel (liens) are added; the organisation file lists only credit analysts, the controller and account managers for this process.
The organisation file links this process only to invoices and payments; disputes also feed back to fin-field-ticket-to-invoice as credit memos, which is not shown as a business object link.
Lien registration is shown for Alberta wells; BC has a similar Builders Lien Act. Shares of liens and write-offs are low ordinary-year values; 2020 had more.

The simulated median (about 15 days, p90 about 43) is below the 21-day estimate: items already approved and scheduled for payment clear in about a week and pull the median down. The estimate is unsourced, so the gap is left.
